question: Why did official run 92220c94fd25 score 7/10 where the previous main scored 10/10 three times, and which merged change caused it?
answer: No merged change caused it. All three failures are browser-process faults on the hosted runner inside one 19.3 s window; the same application passes the same unchanged public tests 25 of 25 locally in the calibrated hosted configuration.

failure_mechanism.summary: Three tests in flight during a 17 s window died to renderer faults; the seven that ran after the window all passed and were faster than the 10/10 run fastest test.

failures.test: REQ-1.1: successfully register a new account and remain signed in
failures.reading: A trivial evaluate (element.tagName.toLowerCase()) hung on an already-resolved visible element. Application code cannot make that hang; the renderer was wedged.

failures.test: REQ-1.2: sign in with a valid username and password
failures.reading: Reported after 1,193 ms against a 10,000 ms expect timeout, on the same machine inside the same window; the expect did not run its timeout.

failures.test: REQ-1.2: sign in with a case-insensitive email and password
failures.reading: Unambiguous Chromium renderer crash. Duration exceeds the 10 s test timeout by 5 s, which is teardown also hanging on the dead target.

failure_mechanism.note: Every passing test in the 7/10 run is faster than the fastest test of the 10/10 run, so the application is not heavier or slower.

local_replay.configuration: harness_lab/local_gate.py host mode: application in a 1 CPU / 256 MB container behind the volo launcher, Playwright workers 4, fullyParallel false, 10 s timeouts, retries 0, video off, trace on for diagnosis only
local_replay.application: workspace of run 92220c94fd25, backend/data stripped by the gate as usual

attribution.verdict: None of PR #17, PR #19 or PR #11 produced the failing behaviour.

pr_17_small_board_tokens.generation_system_prompt: byte-identical between the two runs, 3,996 characters both
pr_17_small_board_tokens.requirement_semantics: preserved verbatim, including the REQ-1 scenario "系统保存账号并创建会话，首页显示用户名和\u201c退出登录\u201d，刷新页面后仍保持登录"
pr_17_small_board_tokens.evidence_strength: strong - the removed fields were empty or redundant on a fresh small board

pr_19_repair_loop.observed: The first self-check failed 3 of 11; the repair edited checks/requirements.cjs only, inserting page.goto("/") before three page.click("a[href=/register|/login]") calls.
pr_19_repair_loop.assessment: The edit makes the model check navigate the way the official helper does (openRegister and openLogin both call openHome first). It corrected a defect in the model own check and masked nothing in the application.
pr_19_repair_loop.reference_run_shape: identical - first self-check failed, one repair round, second passed, 3 model calls total
pr_19_repair_loop.evidence_strength: strong - the repair diff is in the trace and is three navigation insertions

pr_11_observer_model.images_sent: identical, same three sha256 values and same transformed sizes
pr_11_observer_model.assessment: Both observations describe the same header links, nav bar, form fields and buttons. Neither mentions signed-in state, because all three reference screenshots are of the signed-out site. Nothing in either text touches the failing behaviour.
pr_11_observer_model.evidence_strength: strong for exoneration, one sample for any quality claim

attribution.sampling_caveat: One official run is one sample. A 7/10 and a 10/10 on this board differ by three tests that died to browser faults, which the bench has now shown at least once.

fix.change: The prepared check harness launches one Chromium for the whole check run and gives each check its own browser context, instead of launching and closing a browser per check. The browser is closed in a node:test after hook, a crashed browser is relaunched, and context teardown no longer masks the authored failure.
fix.rationale: The only lever in our control on this failure class. The run last act before the official suite was its own self-check launching 11 Chromium processes in 7.9 s, finishing 2.1 s before the official suite started in the same container.

measurement.subject: the failed run own checks/requirements.cjs, 11 checks, against its own application

fix.unit_tests: tests/test_browser_lifecycle.py, 6 cases: one browser for three checks with a context each, single close after the last check, a failing check still releasing both, relaunch after a browser crash, missing Playwright still failing the check, and an installed Chromium launched once for three checks.
fix.what_it_does_not_claim: This does not prove the renderer faults were caused by self-check browser pressure, and it cannot, from one run. It removes a measured 11-to-1 process churn immediately before evaluation. Confirmation would be a run of official trials on this board with no browser fault in the evaluation window.

confirming_evidence_wanted: Official Ticket Booking runs from this main with the fix, looking only at whether any evaluation-window browser fault appears; a pass rate change alone would not separate the fix from generation variance.
A local generation with PR #11 reverted to kimi-k3 would test the observer question, which this run does not answer either way.
